excerpt: Rebel Foods runs delivery-only restaurant brands such as Faasos, Behrouz Biryani and Oven Story from 450+ cloud kitchens. Founded in 2011.
content:
Rebel Foods runs restaurant brands that exist mainly for online delivery, cooked in shared cloud kitchens rather than dine-in outlets. Its website lists Faasos, Behrouz, Oven Story, The Good Bowl, Sweet Truth, Lunch Box, Mandarin Oak, Firangi Bake and The Biryani Life, and calls the company the world's largest chain of internet restaurants. Entrepreneur India also lists Wendy's among its brands in India.

Entrepreneur India reported that Rebel Foods was founded in Mumbai in 2011 by Jaydeep Barman, its cofounder and CEO, and Kallol Banerjee, and that it runs more than 450 cloud kitchens across India, the Middle East and North Africa, Indonesia and the UK. The company began as Faasos, which remains one of its brands.

In December 2024 Rebel Foods raised USD 210 million in a Series G round led by Temasek, with existing investor Evolvence, combining new shares with the sale of existing ones, according to Entrackr. Entrackr also reported FY24 revenue from operations of Rs 1,420 crore and losses narrowed by more than 42% to Rs 378 crore. Entrepreneur India said the company was preparing for a possible listing within 12 to 18 months.

Rebel Foods doesn't sell memberships; you order its brands through food-delivery apps or its own channels and pay menu prices, which vary by city. This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product for this page, and nothing here is paid placement.
